description: The fresh-id minter alone, with no reduction around it (README.md §2). Case 15 pins the derived-id PROPERTY through a rewrite, which is the right test but the wrong debugger: an implementation whose ids come out different there cannot tell a wrong digest from a wrong rule, a wrong ordinal order, or a wrong pair ordering. These vectors are key-in / id-out. Each entry names the two redex glyphs, the two parent ids, and the 1-based ordinal within that rewrite; the expectation is the id. The vectors are chosen to pin the parts an implementer can get wrong independently: both components are sorted, so swapping the glyphs or swapping the parents changes nothing (vectors 1-3 are the same id); the two sorted components are NOT interchangeable with each other, so a flat sort of all four strings is wrong (vector 4 differs from vector 1 despite the same multiset); the ordinal is part of the key and 1-based (vectors 5-6); the separator is US (U+001F), so a key built with any other joiner fails everything; and the rendering is `_r` + the first 12 lowercase hex digits of the SHA-256, i.e. the first 6 bytes of the digest, big-endian as hex is written.
